title: How an anaerobic digester turns waste into biogas

explain.say: An anaerobic digester is a sealed, warm tank where bacteria break down food waste, manure or sewage without any oxygen, rather like the inside of a cow's stomach.

faq.a: Anaerobic means without oxygen. In a sealed tank, different groups of bacteria break food waste or manure down step by step into simpler substances, finally making methane and carbon dioxide.

Mostly methane, about 50 to 70 percent, and carbon dioxide, with small amounts of water vapour and hydrogen sulphide, which smells of rotten eggs. Methane is the same burnable gas found in natural gas.
asks: Is biogas the same as natural gas?

faq.a: It can be burned in an engine to make electricity and heat, cleaned into biomethane and fed into the gas grid or used as vehicle fuel, or burned for cooking on small farm digesters.

faq.q: What happens to the leftover digestate?
faq.a: Digestate keeps most of the nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium from the original waste, so farmers spread it on fields as fertiliser instead of buying chemical ones.
Yes. The carbon in it came from plants that took carbon dioxide from the air recently, and new waste is made every day. Capturing methane from waste also stops a powerful greenhouse gas escaping.
asks: Is biogas good for the environment?

facts: Biogas is typically about 50 to 70 percent methane, with most of the rest carbon dioxide.
Over a century, methane traps roughly 28 times more heat than the same mass of carbon dioxide.

quiz.say: Why must an anaerobic digester be sealed?

options.show: The bacteria that make methane work without oxygen
options.say: The bacteria that make methane work without oxygen

quiz.why: Methane-making microbes only work without oxygen, and sealing also traps the gas so it can be collected.

wrong.1: Digesters are kept warm, but sealing is about keeping oxygen out and gas in.
wrong.2: The digestate stays in the tank whether or not it is sealed.
